verifier_note: Checked every recipe's warrant sources by direct retrieval, never from memory: docs.rs pages at the pinned versions (wasmtime 49.0.1, godot 0.5.5, rapier3d-f64 0.35.3, parry3d-f64 0.30.2, glamx 0.3.1, bytemuck 1.25.2, cbindgen 0.29.4), official docs (wasmtime.dev, doc.rust-lang.org/stable, docs.godotengine.org 4.7/4.5, dev.epicgames.com, component-model.bytecodealliance.org, godot-rust.github.io), raw crate/GitHub source (godot-wasm store.h/SConstruct/utils.py at two refs, glamx eigen3.rs, parry mass_properties.rs, cbindgen CHANGES, Cargo.toml source views), GitHub release pages via gh CLI (wasmtime v49.0.0/v49.0.1/v48.0.3, wasmer v7.4.2, WAMR-2.4.5, wasm3 v0.9.0, jco-v1.35.0, wit-bindgen v0.62.0), two godot-proposals issues, and si-rpg-engine itself at the pinned commit f84c98b (build.mjs, FLAGS.md, README.md, solver/src/lib.rs, rapier_law.rs, .cargo/config.toml, trace-line.mjs, first-difference.js, docs/PHASE-2.md, the product-alignment dispatch). I ran all 17 of the lane's checks through the real pinned rustc 1.98.1 plus the real rapier3d-f64/parry3d-f64/bytemuck rlibs and node v22.22.3 via compile_oracle.py: 17/17 passed with exact stdout, exact compile_fail error codes (E0277, E0080), and exact wasm export/import lists, including a real rapier3d-f64 physics run whose collision event lands at quantum 20 exactly as claimed and a native/wasm FNV match (4769065195358558711) that is genuinely opt-level-3-native-vs-wasm, not asserted. I independently reproduced the JS negative-zero claim on this rig's node v22.22.3 (String(-0), (-0).toFixed(3), JSON.stringify(-0) all print without a minus sign) and confirmed wasm3's and godot-wasm's release histories have no tagged release hiding between the cited versions. I also diffed the pinned commit against main (17 commits ahead as of this sweep) specifically hunting for the stale-engine_note pattern another lane in this sweep flagged: docs/PHASE-2.md did change on main, but only in the T2/T7 area; the T1 and T3 rows every host-embedding recipe cites are byte-for-byte identical, and the new docs/dispatch-t3-platforms.md corroborates rather than contradicts recipe 2's 'T3 will refuse growable memory' claim (it reveals the pinned binary's allocator did still call memory.grow at f84c98b, which is exactly the live risk recipes 1 and 2 tell hosts to defend against). Nothing in the ten recipes was false, unsupported, or mismatched between check and prose; every one of roughly 74 warrant sources resolved and supported its claim verbatim. What failed: nothing verifiable failed. The systemic weakness is not an error but a shelf-life one: the lane's authority rests on two extremely fast-moving artifacts, Wasmtime (a new major every month; 49.0.1 and 48.0.3 both shipped the identical fuel-spend security fix on 2026-09-24, one day before this sweep) and si-rpg-engine itself (17 commits and a same-day PHASE-2.md amendment within the pinned commit's own calendar day) - so 'solid' here means solid against today's ground truth, not against a stable target, and the runtime-config recipe plus every engine_note will need the 30-day freshness re-check the studio's own memory rule already prescribes sooner than most lanes would.
